## Rows: 717 Columns: 9
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr (4): institution_name, city, state, institution_type
## dbl (5): id, enrollment, endowment_fy_20, hbcu_indicator, carnegie_category
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
# a glimpse of the data
# for this analysis, do NOT convert chr to factors (do not worry about this)
dplyr::glimpse(ntse_tbl)
## Rows: 717
## Columns: 9
## $ id                <dbl> 166027, 229090, 130794, 243744, 186131, 166683, 2150…
## $ institution_name  <chr> "Harvard University", "University of Texas System", …
## $ city              <chr> "Cambridge", "Austin", "New Haven", "Stanford", "Pri…
## $ state             <chr> "MA", "TX", "CT", "CA", "NJ", "MA", "PA", "TX", "MI"…
## $ institution_type  <chr> "Private college/university endowment", "Public coll…
## $ enrollment        <dbl> 24610, 190308, 13539, 16793, 7795, 11415, 23770, 122…
## $ endowment_fy_20   <dbl> 40575027, 31958313, 31201700, 28948000, 26558643, 18…
## $ hbcu_indicator    <dbl> 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2…
## $ carnegie_category <dbl> 4, 0, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 0, 4, 0, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4…
ntse_tbl$id = as.factor(ntse_tbl$id)
ntse_tbl$hbcu_indicator = as.factor(ntse_tbl$hbcu_indicator)
ntse_tbl$carnegie_category = as.factor(ntse_tbl$carnegie_category)
